To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have recruited a sample of 375 individuals from 21 extended families across Mexico, that we have measured a wide range of phenotypes related to CVD, and that these phenotypes are heritable.
we found significant heritability of metabolic disease–related phenotypes and significant genetic correlations between measures of adipose and metabolic phenotypes in Mexico.

the heritability and genetic correlations of metabolic disease-related phenotypes are consistent with the definition of the metabolic syndrome and that the design of this study offers excellent power for gene discovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic epidemiology, etiology and pathogenesis, and prevention and control of cardiovascular disease (CVD), particularly in the Republic of México, and the role of metabolic syndrome in CVD risk.
identifying the genetic factors that contribute to the development of common diseases.
understanding the genetic basis of common diseases in the Mexican population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GEMM family study has provided a preliminary report of the heritability of several metabolic disease-related phenotypes in Mexico.
this study design has the potential to provide a significant contribution to gene discovery for metabolic disease.

there are significant heritable components to the major risk factors for CVD and type 2 diabetes in Mexican families and that there are significant genetic and environmental correlations among these risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GEMM family study is the first study to estimate heritabilities for a number of metabolic disease-related phenotypes, and the first study to report genetic correlation estimates for metabolic disease-related phenotypic traits in Mexico.
we have successfully recruited a large sample for the study of metabolic disease and its genetic epidemiology in Mexico.
we have successfully implemented a study design for the genetic epidemiology study of complex metabolic disease in Mexico, and the preliminary results are promising.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have established the first large-scale family study of metabolic disease in Mexico.
we have demonstrated the feasibility and value of conducting a family study of metabolic disease in Mexico.
the GEMM study design is feasible in Mexico.
